import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mathoverflow 21003

Is there any polynomial $f(x, y) \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y]$ such that
$f : \mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ is a bijection?

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/21003](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/21003)
asked by user [*Z.H.*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/5098/z-h)
-/

open scoped Polynomial


namespace Mathoverflow21003

/--
Is there any polynomial $f(x, y) \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y]$ such that
$f : \mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ is a bijection?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
theorem mathoverflow_21003 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ, Function.Bijective fun x ↦ f.eval x := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow21003

reformulations.difference: The source uses the domain ℚ × ℚ; Lean evaluates a polynomial in MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ on assignments of type Fin 2 → ℚ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The equivalence finTwoArrowEquiv ℚ sends x to (x 0, x 1), with inverse (a,b) ↦ ![a,b]. For each polynomial f, evaluation on pairs is exactly the Lean evaluation function precomposed with this inverse. Precomposition with an equivalence preserves and reflects bijectivity, so existential quantification over f gives the same question. Both the per-polynomial and existential equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry or dependence on the problem theorem.

sources_consulted: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/21003 — original question, all three answers, and comments.

Bjorn Poonen, Multivariable polynomial injections on rational numbers, §1, Theorem 1.1 and remarks; https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.3961 and the v2 LaTeX source downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/0902.3961.

Giulio Bresciani, A higher dimensional Hilbert irreducibility theorem, introduction, Theorem C, and the polynomial-bijections section; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.01090 and the v3 LaTeX source downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2101.01090.
https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2019/06/08/ruling-out-polynomial-bijections-over-the-rationals-via-bombieri-lang/ — main post, February 2021 update, and relevant discussion of Bresciani’s result.
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the cited question. Rational coefficients, both rational inputs, the rational codomain, bijectivity, and the scope of answer(sorry) all agree. Lean checks confirmed ordinary polynomial evaluation, rejection of constant candidates, and that coordinate projections are surjective but not injective. The scratch file compiled successfully. The research-open status is consistent with the consulted sources: Bresciani’s nonexistence theorem assumes weak Bombieri–Lang for surfaces and does not settle the unconditional question.
